title: Exact values and approximations

match.reason: The bank point teaches the central difference method for estimating derivatives, which is a different idea from keeping exact values such as √2 and π separate from their decimal approximations.

draft.title: Exact values and approximations
card: An exact value is written precisely, such as √2, π or 9π. The decimals of √2 and π go on forever without repeating, so no decimal can write them exactly.
A decimal such as 1.414 is only an approximation of √2. Check: 1.414² = 1.999396, not 2. We write √2 ≈ 1.414, where ≈ means is approximately equal to.
A circle with radius 3 has area π × 3² = 9π. This is exact. 28.27 is an approximation of it.
Leave an answer in exact form when asked, and use a decimal only when an approximate value is wanted.
draft.remember: An exact value is kept as it is. A decimal is only an approximation of it.

a.q: Which is the exact area of a circle with radius 4?
a.why: The area is π × 4² = 16π, which is kept as it is. The other three are decimals that only approximate 16π, which is about 50.265.
a.clue: Which answer has no rounding in it?

b.q: Mia says the diagonal of a square with side 1 is 1.41. The exact diagonal is √2. Which statement is correct?
opts: 1.41 is an approximation of the exact value √2
1.41 is exact because the decimal stops after 2 places
√2 is an approximation of the exact value 1.41
1.41 and √2 are equal, so Mia has given the exact value
b.why: √2 is the exact value, and 1.41 is a rounded decimal close to it. Check: 1.41² = 1.9881, not 2. A decimal that stops is still not equal to √2.
b.clue: Square 1.41 and see if you get exactly 2.

b.best: 1.41 is an approximation of the exact value √2
